evidence.claim: Dutch Bros operates and franchises drive-thru shops and sells/distributes coffee and coffee-related products; as of December 31, 2025, it had 1,136 shops in 25 U.S. states, including 811 company-operated and 325 franchised shops.
Dutch Bros identifies its competitive set as national and regional coffee chains, local specialty coffee shops, regional drive-thru beverage chains, drive-thru QSRs, and convenience stores.

Keurig Dr Pepper describes itself as a North American beverage company that manufactures, markets, distributes, and sells hot and cold beverages and single-serve brewing systems; its portfolio includes Green Mountain Coffee Roasters and the Keurig brewing system.
KDP's 2025 10-K defines a planned separation of its beverage and coffee portfolios into two independent publicly traded companies, announced on August 25, 2025.

Westrock Coffee describes itself as an integrated coffee, tea, flavors, extracts, and ingredients solutions provider serving retail, foodservice, restaurant, convenience store, travel center, CPG, and hospitality industries.

Westrock reported 2025 Beverage Solutions net sales of $908.4 million versus $659.4 million in 2024, with growth attributed partly to coffee and tea products, single-serve cup volumes, roast-and-ground volumes, commodity coffee price pass-through, tariffs, and Conway extract/ready-to-drink facility ramp.

Middleby's commercial foodservice equipment portfolio includes numerous restaurant equipment brands, including beverage- or drink-adjacent names such as Bloomfield, Concordia, Deutsche Beverage, Follett, Icetro, Marco, Synesso, Taylor, Toastmaster, and Wunder-Bar.

Toast's 2025 annual report says its POS and restaurant operations offerings are built to reduce time to take orders and include POS terminals, handheld devices, self-service kiosks, kitchen display systems, loyalty, marketing, gift cards, first-party online ordering, and delivery integrations.

memory_update.text: Add BROS as direct beverage-led restaurant pure-play for the coffee/beverage/daypart node; monitor transactions, same-shop sales, and expansion economics rather than treating it only as a coffee-chain comp.
Add KDP as a large-cap adjacent supplier/brand platform with hot/cold beverages, single-serve coffee systems, and a possible catalyst for clearer coffee mapping through portfolio separation.

Add WEST as a below-$1B exception because its integrated coffee, tea, extract, flavor, RTD, sourcing, and foodservice/restaurant exposure make it unusually close to the upstream beverage innovation chokepoint.

Add MIDD as second-order restaurant equipment exposure where beverage throughput, ice, refrigeration, dispensers, automation, and drink consistency may become a capex bottleneck for beverage-led concepts.
Add TOST as adjacent software infrastructure for beverage-led restaurants because order speed, loyalty, first-party digital ordering, and data-driven retention can be key frequency enablers.

Need a follow-up pass on private/non-US chokepoints: BUNN, Franke, JDE Peet's legacy assets, private flavor houses, commercial ice/dispensing equipment, and loyalty vendors such as Paytronix that are not directly US-listed.

node: Coffee, beverages, snacks, and daypart innovation
summary: Expanded universe for the beverage-led restaurant node emphasizes direct beverage concepts plus second-order suppliers that may benefit from frequency, throughput, loyalty, cold/functional beverage innovation, and coffee cost pass-through. The most underappreciated mappings appear to be integrated coffee/beverage ingredient suppliers, restaurant equipment vendors tied to speed and drink prep, and restaurant software platforms tied to loyalty/order-ahead. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation.
